hn.originalTitle: Perplexity launches AI agents for work
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Teammates are agents for complex, ongoing work

Perplexity pioneered the first web-capable AI assistant in July 2025 in the Comet browser . It was useful for booking restaurants, shopping, and dozens of uses popular with personal agents today.

Since then, model capabilities have advanced dramatically. And Perplexity Computer is where millions of people and companies do serious work with accurate AI. Personal agents need to be purpose-built for work.

Today, we’re launching teammates, personal agents that can take on that long-running work. They plan and coordinate projects, switch gears as priorities change, and present results for review. Users can inspect and guide their work along the way.

Computer can handle complex projects, but setting up an agent to own ongoing work required planning. Teammates build on the power of Computer, and work inside Computer with all of your tools and files.

A teammate coordinates Computer sessions and other teammates to keep projects moving. They remember and learn as they work across different workstreams like marketing, sales, support, operations, or finance.

Ongoing project ownership

Teammates represent a new way of working with AI. Users can delegate ongoing actions to teammates so people can focus on outcomes rather than coordinating every task. Built on Perplexity’s focus on accuracy and Computer’s multi-model capabilities, teammates plan the work, check results along the way, and bring completed work back for review.

Teammates can investigate issues, research a market, or test improvements to a product, among other tasks. They remember project goals, task history, and shared files across runs. Each new task a teammate takes on builds on the work already done.

Proactive monitoring and follow-through

Teammates monitor ongoing work and follow up as things change. They investigate and act without waiting for a fresh query.

For example, a sales teammate notices when a regular customer stops transacting. The teammate reviews their order history and support issues and investigates what changed.

Then, it creates an offer relevant to that customer or flags any issues to resolve before reaching out. It shares progress updates and approval requests until it completes the work.

Teammates also remember past work and apply feedback to future tasks. If a user tells an operations teammate an agency needs two weeks’ notice, it factors that lead time into future project schedules.

Shared direction across teams

Teammates can work across teams. Add a teammate to a Slack channel and colleagues can hand it work or ask for updates on a task.

Teammates can also pass work to each other. One teammate finds bugs on a website and passes its findings along to another to prepare fixes.

Coordination across tools and tasks

Teammates build on the projects , skills, and memory already available in Computer. For example, a sales teammate can use a project’s existing account research and sales goals, follow a skill for writing outreach, and run a weekly automation to review the pipeline.

It brings those pieces together to identify stalled conversations, prepare follow-ups for review, and apply the results to the next week’s work.

Isolated environments and access controls

Teammates build on Computer’s existing tool and project permissions. Each teammate runs in a separate environment, with browser sessions separate from other teammates.

Saved credentials are encrypted and entered securely. Users can review completed work, take over the desktop, or redirect a teammate as it works.

Workflows across the business

Teammates handle ongoing work across business functions. These examples show how monitoring, investigation, and follow-through work together:

Marketing: A marketing teammate manages social posts, email campaigns, ads, search engine optimisation, and review notes, creating new ads based on what’s working. It monitors campaign performance and competitors’ promotions, drafts fixes when results slip, and suggests responses when competitors change prices.

Sales: A sales teammate finds opportunities in customer enquiries, past purchases, and unfinished conversations. It prepares outreach and quotes, follows up on replies, and flags support issues that need to be resolved before reaching out.

hn.titleZh: Perplexity 推出人工智慧工作代理
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
队友是复杂、持续工作的代理人 Perplexity 于 2025 年 7 月在 Comet 浏览器中率先推出了第一个具有网络功能的 AI 助手。它對於預訂餐廳、購物以及當今個人代理商流行的數十種用途非常有用。从那时起，模型功能取得了显着进步。 Perplexity Computer 是數百萬人和公司利用準確的人工智慧進行認真工作的地方。個人代理需要專為工作而設計。今天，我們正在推出可以承擔這項長期工作的隊友、個人代理。他們規劃和協調項目，隨著優先事項的變化而改變方向，並提交結果供審查。用户可以一路检查和指导他们的工作。计算机可以处理复杂的项目，但设置代理来负责正在进行的工作需要规划。團隊成員利用電腦的強大功能，並使用您的所有工具和文件在電腦內工作。一名隊友協調電腦會話和其他隊友以保持專案順利進行。他们在营销、销售、支持、运营或财务等不同工作流程中工作时会记住并学习。持續的專案所有權 Teammates 代表了一種使用 AI 的新方式。使用者可以將正在進行的操作委託給團隊成員，這樣人們就可以專注於結果，而不是協調每項任務。

基於 Perplexity 對準確性的關注和電腦的多模型功能，團隊成員可以規劃工作、檢查結果，並將完成的工作帶回進行審查。團隊成員可以調查問題、研究市場或測試產品的改進等任務。他們記住專案目標、任務歷史記錄以及運行期間的共用檔案。隊友承擔的每一項新任務都建立在已經完成的工作的基礎上。主動監控與跟進 隊友監控正在進行的工作並在情況發生變化時進行跟進。他們不等待新的詢問就進行調查並採取行動。例如，銷售團隊成員會注意到老客戶停止交易。隊友查看他們的訂單歷史記錄和支援問題並調查發生了什麼變化。然後，它會建立與該客戶相關的報價或標記在聯繫之前需要解決的任何問題。它共享進度更新和批准請求，直到完成工作。隊友也會記住過去的工作並將回饋應用於未來的任務。如果使用者告訴營運團隊成員某個機構需要提前兩週通知，則會將交付時間納入未來的專案計畫中。跨團隊分享方向 隊友可以跨團隊工作。將隊友加入 Slack 頻道，同事可以交給它工作或請求任務的更新。隊友也可以互相傳遞工作。

一名隊友發現網站上的錯誤，並將其發現傳遞給另一名隊友以準備修復。跨工具和任務的協調 隊友以電腦中已有的項目、技能和記憶為基礎。例如，銷售團隊成員可以使用專案的現有客戶研究和銷售目標，遵循撰寫外展的技能，並運行每週自動化來審查管道。它將這些碎片整合在一起，以識別停滯的對話，準備後續審查，並將結果應用到下週的工作中。隔離的環境和存取控制隊友建立在電腦現有的工具和項目權限之上。每個隊友都在單獨的環境中運行，瀏覽器會話與其他隊友分開。保存的憑證經過加密並安全輸入。使用者可以查看已完成的工作、接管桌面或在工作時重新導向團隊成員。跨業務的工作流程 團隊成員處理跨業務職能的持續工作。這些範例顯示了監控、調查和後續工作如何協同工作： 行銷：行銷團隊成員管理社群貼文、電子郵件行銷活動、廣告、搜尋引擎優化和審核筆記，根據有效內容建立新廣告。它監控活動績效和競爭對手的促銷活動，在結果下滑時草擬修復方案，並在競爭對手改變價格時提出應對措施。

销售：销售团队成员在客户询问、过去的购买情况和未完成的对话中寻找机会。它準備外展和報價，跟進回复，並標記在外展之前需要解決的支援問題。客戶支援：客戶支援團隊成員審查前一天的投訴，總結趨勢，並標記需要執行長親自回覆的案例。它起草这些回复，跟进内部团队的修复情况，并跟踪每个问题

hn.originalTitle: "No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run businesses
hn.sourceOriginalText:
"No human at the helm": Delaware plan would let AI agents run entire businesses - Ars Technica

A Delaware proposal to let companies be operated by AI agents would help the firms’ human owners evade legal responsibility for reckless and harmful actions taken by the AI, US Rep. James Comer (R-Ky.) told Delaware Governor Matt Meyer in a letter yesterday.

Comer, chairman of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, told Meyer that the committee “seeks assistance obtaining documents related to your state administration’s efforts to establish a new form of corporate entity to be known as an Artificial Intelligence Company (AIC).”

Comer said the proposal is ripe for abuse. “We are concerned that Delaware’s AIC proposal could be used to protect powerful AI companies and their investors from responsibility for reckless harmful actions, while also protecting non-transparent forces seeking anticompetitive regulatory capture behind state AI initiatives,” Comer’s letter said.

Comer suggested he may propose a federal law that would limit states’ regulatory authority. He said the committee’s probe of Delaware’s plan would “inform possible federal legislative efforts including proposals to appropriately limit state AI regulatory initiatives.” Citing the Oversight Committee’s “jurisdiction to study intergovernmental relationships including those of states,” Comer asked for documents related to development of the proposal and potential AI safety risks.

AI-run companies could operate in just about any industry except banking. “An AIC may have any lawful purpose, regardless of whether for profit, except for the business of banking,” according to a draft bill that may be submitted to the Delaware State Legislature.

The draft bill says AI agents could be “designated to manage the business and affairs, and to conduct the business, of the AIC.” The bill proposes a “regulatory sandbox” that would exist for 30 months to test the idea. Allowing AI-run companies would bring more revenue via taxes and fees to Delaware, which is already a top destination for business entities of all sizes.

“The answer is to wrap AI in legal form”

In July 2026, Delaware Secretary of State Charuni Patibanda-Sanchez co-wrote an op-ed in Fortune announcing the proposal. The op-ed said that “nothing in the law of several states clearly prevents an AI agent from operating a company with no human at the helm,” and that states should develop legal frameworks for autonomous software that is able to contract, pay suppliers, and make transactions with no human involvement.

“The answer is not to try to prohibit the activity; any effort to do so is just as unlikely to succeed as the technology and its enablers are likely to push the boundaries of the law,” the op-ed said. “The answer is to wrap AI in legal form. Give an autonomous system a recognizable legal identity and you make it legible to law. You create a deﬁned target to which responsibility and damages can attach. You make the agent’s conduct visible, traceable, and accountable.”

The op-ed explained how an AI-run company will shield humans from legal liabilities:

A Delaware AIC will be a separate legal entity whose day-to-day aﬀairs are managed by an AI agent rather than a person. At the agent’s direction, the AIC can sue and be sued in its own name, hold and dispose of property, and incur obligations. It has a single member, a person or an entity, responsible for keeping the AIC adequately capitalized, and the AIC must keep a log of its activities. That member is shielded from the AIC’s debts, except where it fails to capitalize the company or uses it to commit fraud or a willful violation of law.

Under the proposed law, the “member” is an individual or a corporation that would fund the AI-run company and benefit from any profits, but designate an AI agent to manage the actual business. The draft bill says, “The member is not liable for any act or omission that the AIC takes or fails to take, or that another person takes or fails to take at the direction of the AIC.” There are exceptions for when a person uses the AI-run company “to engage in fraud or any willful violation of law,” or “caused or allowed the AIC to conduct business when the member knew or should have known the conduct was outside the AIC’s statement of purpose.”

hn.titleZh: 「無人掌舵」：特拉華州計畫將讓人工智慧代理經營業務
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
「無人掌舵」：特拉華州的計劃將讓人工智慧代理商經營整個企業 - Ars Technica 美國眾議員詹姆斯·科默（肯塔基州共和黨人）在昨天的一封信中告訴特拉華州州長馬特·邁耶，特拉華州提議讓人工智能代理運營公司，這將有助於公司的人類所有者逃避因人工智能魯莽和有害行為而承擔的法律責任。眾議院監督和政府改革委員會主席科默告訴邁耶，該委員會「尋求協助，獲取與你們州政府努力建立一種新形式的公司實體（即人工智慧公司（AIC））相關的文件。」科默表示，該提案被濫用的時機已經成熟。科默在信中表示：「我們擔心特拉華州的 AIC 提案可能會被用來保護強大的人工智慧公司及其投資者免受魯莽有害行為的責任，同時也保護在州人工智慧計劃背後尋求反競爭監管的非透明勢力。」科默表示，他可能會提出一項限制各州監管權力的聯邦法律。

他表示，委員會對特拉華州計劃的調查將“為可能的聯邦立法工作提供信息，包括適當限制州人工智能監管舉措的提案。”科默援引監督委員會的“研究政府間關係（包括國家間關係）的管轄權”，要求提供與提案製定和潛在人工智能安全風險相關的文件。人工智慧營運的公司幾乎可以在銀行業以外的任何行業運作。根據可能提交給特拉華州立法機構的一項法案草案，「AIC 可以有任何合法目的，無論是否以營利為目的，但銀行業務除外」。該法案草案稱，人工智慧代理可以「被指定管理 AIC 的業務和事務，並開展業務」。該法案提出了一個為期 30 個月的「監管沙箱」來測試這個想法。允許人工智慧營運的公司將透過稅收和費用為特拉華州帶來更多收入，特拉華州已經是各種規模的商業實體的首選目的地。 「答案是以法律形式包裝人工智慧」 2026 年 7 月，特拉華州國務卿查魯尼·帕蒂班達-桑切斯 (Charuni Patibanda-Sanchez) 在《財富》雜誌上共同撰寫了一篇專欄文章，宣布了這一提議。

這篇專欄文章稱，“幾個州的法律中沒有明確禁止人工智慧代理商經營一家無人掌舵的公司”，各州應該為自主軟體製定法律框架，使其能夠在無人參與的情況下與供應商簽訂合約、向供應商付款並進行交易。 「答案不是試圖禁止這種活動；任何這樣做的努力都不太可能成功，因為該技術及其推動者可能會突破法律的界限，」專欄文章說。 「答案是以法律形式包裝人工智慧。給一個自治系統一個可識別的法律身份，讓它在法律上清晰可辨。你創建一個明確的目標，責任和損害可以附加到該目標上。你讓代理的行為可見、可追踪和負責。」這篇專欄文章解釋了人工智能運營的公司將如何保護人類免受法律責任：特拉華州 AIC 將是一個獨立的人工智能實體，其日常事務由人工智能負責管理。根據代理人的指示，AIC 可以以自己的名義起訴和被起訴，持有和處置財產，並承擔義務。它有一個成員、一個人或一個實體，負責保持 AIC 充足的資本，並且 AIC 必須保留其活動日誌。

該成員不受 AIC 債務的影響，除非該成員未能對公司進行資本化或利用其進行欺詐或故意違法。根据拟议的法律，“成员”是指为人工智能运营的公司提供资金并从任何利润中受益的个人或公司，但指定人工智能代理人来管理实际业务。该法案草案称，“会员对工商局采取或未采取的任何作为或不作为，或者他人按照工商局的指示采取或未采取的任何作为或不作为不承担责任。”也有例外情况，即某人利用人工智能运营的公司“从事欺诈或任何故意违法行为”，或“在成员知道或应该知道该行为超出 AIC 目的声明的情况下导致或允许 AIC 开展业务”。科默援引 Patibanda-Sanchez 的声明，写道，一家人工智能运营的公司将为“利用 AIC 的个人或实体提供责任保护，使其免受控制 AIC 所造成的对业务合作伙伴、消费者和公众的潜在伤害”。

hn.originalTitle: AI coding agent setups from 663 Hacker News comments
hn.sourceOriginalText:
AI coding agent setups from a 663-comment Ask HN: tool counts…

AI coding agent setups from a 663-comment Ask HN: tool counts and 7 patterns to copy

On November 4, 2026, an Ask HN thread asked developers for their current AI agent setup, and 663 comments came back. We read every one, counted the tools 424 people say they use, and turned the most detailed setups into seven patterns you can start using today.

424 of the 530 people who commented named at least one AI tool they use. Claude Code leads with 180 people, then Codex with 103. We counted on November 6, 2026.

Most people mix vendors. 120 of the 424 named both a Claude product and an OpenAI product, and 156 use two or more coding agents.

Open-weight models do real work here. 148 people named DeepSeek, Qwen, GLM, Kimi or another open-weight or local model, and 58 of them named no Claude or OpenAI tool at all.

The most detailed setups share a few habits: several agents at once, each in its own git worktree; a fresh second reviewer on every change; and a VM or container around any agent allowed to run without asking.

Even heavy users say the basics matter most: write down what done looks like, and review the work before it ships.

What the thread asked and who answered

On November 4, 2026, the user eggbrain posted "Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?" It asked five questions: which AI plans people pay for, which other models they use, which coding harness (the program that runs the agent) they use, whether they use tools that run many agents at once, and whether they use always-on agent platforms.

We fetched the thread on November 6, 2026, at about 9:00 AM MST. It had 534 points and 663 comments from 530 different people. 392 comments were direct answers to the post. The rest were replies.

Three readers each read every comment. For each one they wrote down the tools the person says they use, the tools they only mention, and any signs of an advanced setup, such as parallel agents or a review loop. We then counted people, not comments, so a person who posted five times counts once per tool. All the links for tools and comments named on this page are in the Sources list at the bottom.

The tools, by how many people use them

These are people who say they use each tool, out of the 424 commenters who named at least one. One person can use many tools, so the numbers add up to more than 424. When someone said Claude while talking about coding, the readers counted it as Claude Code. Counted November 6, 2026.

Tool (what it is) People Claude Code (Anthropic coding agent) 180 Claude plan (Pro, Max or Team) 145 Codex (OpenAI coding agent) 103 ChatGPT plan or app 92 Claude Opus (model) 80 DeepSeek (open-weight models) 78 OpenCode (open-source coding agent) 69 Pi (open-source coding agent) 67 OpenRouter (one API for many models) 55 Qwen (open-weight models) 46 GLM from Z.ai (open-weight models) 44 Gemini (Google models and app) 36 Hermes Agent (personal agent) 29 Herdr (runs many agent sessions) 28 GPT models through the API 26 VS Code (editor) 26 GitHub Copilot 22 Claude Sonnet (model) 19 Grok (models and app) 17 tmux (terminal multiplexer) 17 Antigravity (Google agent IDE) 17 Claude Code is the mos.

paustint: parallel agents in long-lived worktrees. They keep numbered worktrees open all the time and run up to eight Claude Code agents on different tasks inside Herdr, which flags the pane that is done or needs them. lazygit handles git. Long jobs go to remote machines over SSH so the laptop can close. A Claude skill reads GitHub Copilot's PR review comments, checks each one, replies and pushes fixes. Why it counts: the whole loop from ticket to reviewed PR, run in parallel.

skwee357: every project in its own VM. Each project runs in a Lima microVM with Claude Code's skip-permissions mode on, 5 to 7 worktrees run side by side in Herdr, and a secrets tool keeps API keys out of the agent's reach. Package installs happen in the VM, never on the laptop. If a VM goes bad, "I just wipe it off, and restart from scratch." Why it counts: full speed with no permission prompts, and a small blast radius.

thefunnyman: plan outside, build inside a box. They use GitHub Copilot CLI under WSL2 with a short list of allowed read-only tools, chat until the plan is right, then have the agent start a Docker Sandbox microVM where it can run without asking. They review the result before any PR goes out. Why it counts: a clean split between a safe place to plan and a sealed place to build.

KronisLV: fresh reviewers until nothing serious is lef

hn.sourceTextZh:
來自 663 條評論的 AI 編碼代理設定 Ask HN：工具計數...來自 663 條評論的 AI 編碼代理設定 Ask HN：工具計數和 7 個要複製的模式 2026 年 11 月 4 日，Ask HN 線程向開發人員詢問他們當前的 AI 代理設置，並返回了 663 條評論。我們閱讀了每一篇文章，統計了 424 人所說的他們使用的工具，並將最詳細的設定轉化為您今天就可以開始使用的七種模式。在 530 名發表評論的人中，有 424 人至少提到了他們使用的一種人工智慧工具。 Claude Code 擁有 180 名員工，Codex 擁有 103 名員工。我們統計的是 2026 年 11 月 6 日。大多數人混合使用供應商。 424 個產品中，有 120 個同時命名為 Claude 產品和 OpenAI 產品，其中 156 個使用兩個或多個編碼代理。開放重量模型在這裡發揮了真正的作用。 148 人提到了 DeepSeek、Qwen、GLM、Kimi 或其他開放權重或本地模型，其中 58 人根本沒有提到 Claude 或 OpenAI 工具。最詳細的設定有一些共同的習慣：同時設定多個代理，每個代理都在自己的 git 工作樹中；每次更改都有新的第二審查員；以及任何代理周圍的虛擬機或容器，無需詢問即可運行。即使是重度使用者也表示基礎知識最重要：寫下完成的內容，並在發布之前進行審查。

該帖子問了什麼以及誰回答了 2026 年 11 月 4 日，用戶 Eggbrain 發布了“問 HN：您當前的 AI 代理設置是什麼？”它提出了五個問題：人們為哪些人工智能計劃付費，他們使用哪些其他模型，他們使用哪種編碼工具（運行代理的程序），他們是否使用同時運行多個代理的工具，以及他們是否使用他們的代理平台。我們於 2026 年 11 月 6 日（MST）上午 9:00 左右獲取了該帖子。它有 534 個點和來自 530 個不同人的 663 條評論。 392則評論是對該貼文的直接回應。剩下的都是回覆。每則評論由三位讀者各自閱讀。對於每一個工具，他們都寫下了該人所說的他們使用的工具、他們只提到的工具以及任何高級設定的跡象，例如並行代理或審查循環。然後我們統計人數，而不是評論，因此發文五次的人每個工具算一次。此頁面上指定的所有工具和評論的連結都位於底部的來源列表中。這些工具，按有多少人使用這些工具 這些人表示自己使用過每種工具，而 424 名評論者中至少提到了一種工具。一個人可以使用多種工具，所以數字加起來超過424。當有人在談論編碼時說Claude時，讀者就把它算作Claude Code。計算日期為 2026 年 11 月 6 日。

工具（是什麼） 人員 Claude Code（人類編碼代理） 180 Claude 計劃（Pro、Max 或 Team） 145 Codex（OpenAI 編碼代理） 103 ChatGPT 計劃或應用程式 92 Claude Opus（模型） 80 DeepSeek（開放權重模型） 78 單元格程式碼（開源） OpenRouter（適用於多種模型的一個 API） 55 Qwen（開放權重模型） 46 來自 Z.ai 的 GLM（開放權重模型） 44 Gemini（Google 模型和應用程式） 36 Hermes Agent（個人代理） 29 Herdr（運行許多代理會話） 28 透過 API 的 GPTHub 模型 26 186 月） 28、4062006 月 282620p 19 Grok（模型和應用程式） 17 tmux （終端多工器） 17 Antigravity（Google代理IDE） 17 克勞德代碼是mos。 paustint：長壽命工作樹中的平行代理。他們始終保持編號的工作樹打開，並在 Herdr 內的不同任務上運行最多八個 Claude Code 代理，這會標記已完成或需要它們的窗格。 Lazygit 處理 git。長作業透過 SSH 傳送到遠端計算機，以便筆記型電腦可以關閉。 Claude 的一項技能是閱讀 GitHub Copilot 的 PR 審核評論，檢查每一則評論，回覆並推送修復。為什麼重要：從票證到審查 PR 的整個循環是並行運行的。 skwee357：每個專案都有自己的虛擬機器。

每個專案都在 Lima microVM 中運行，並啟用 Claude Code 的跳過權限模式，Herdr 中並排運行 5 到 7 個工作樹，並且秘密工具使 API 金鑰遠離代理程式的存取範圍。軟體包安裝發生在虛擬機器中，而不是筆記型電腦上。如果虛擬機器發生故障，「我只需將其清除，然後從頭開始」。為什麼重要：全速，無許可提示，爆炸半徑小。 thefunnyman：在外面規劃，在盒子裡建造。他們使用 WSL2 下的 GitHub Copilot CLI 以及允許的唯讀工具的簡短列表，聊天直到計劃正確，然後讓代理啟動 Docker Sandbox microVM，無需詢問即可運行。他們在發布任何 PR 之前都會審查結果。為什麼重要：安全的規劃地點和密封的建造地點之間的明確劃分。 KronisLV：新的審稿人，直到不留下任何嚴重的問題

Mo is an AI QA engineer for web, iOS and Android apps. Point it at a URL or a build, and it files each bug with repro steps and a screenshot or recording.

hn.originalTitle: Perplexity launches AI agents for work
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Teammates are agents for complex, ongoing work

Perplexity pioneered the first web-capable AI assistant in July 2025 in the Comet browser . It was useful for booking restaurants, shopping, and dozens of uses popular with personal agents today.

Since then, model capabilities have advanced dramatically. And Perplexity Computer is where millions of people and companies do serious work with accurate AI. Personal agents need to be purpose-built for work.

Today, we’re launching teammates, personal agents that can take on that long-running work. They plan and coordinate projects, switch gears as priorities change, and present results for review. Users can inspect and guide their work along the way.

Computer can handle complex projects, but setting up an agent to own ongoing work required planning. Teammates build on the power of Computer, and work inside Computer with all of your tools and files.

A teammate coordinates Computer sessions and other teammates to keep projects moving. They remember and learn as they work across different workstreams like marketing, sales, support, operations, or finance.

Ongoing project ownership

Teammates represent a new way of working with AI. Users can delegate ongoing actions to teammates so people can focus on outcomes rather than coordinating every task. Built on Perplexity’s focus on accuracy and Computer’s multi-model capabilities, teammates plan the work, check results along the way, and bring completed work back for review.

Teammates can investigate issues, research a market, or test improvements to a product, among other tasks. They remember project goals, task history, and shared files across runs. Each new task a teammate takes on builds on the work already done.

Proactive monitoring and follow-through

Teammates monitor ongoing work and follow up as things change. They investigate and act without waiting for a fresh query.

For example, a sales teammate notices when a regular customer stops transacting. The teammate reviews their order history and support issues and investigates what changed.

Then, it creates an offer relevant to that customer or flags any issues to resolve before reaching out. It shares progress updates and approval requests until it completes the work.

Teammates also remember past work and apply feedback to future tasks. If a user tells an operations teammate an agency needs two weeks’ notice, it factors that lead time into future project schedules.

Shared direction across teams

Teammates can work across teams. Add a teammate to a Slack channel and colleagues can hand it work or ask for updates on a task.

Teammates can also pass work to each other. One teammate finds bugs on a website and passes its findings along to another to prepare fixes.

Coordination across tools and tasks

Teammates build on the projects , skills, and memory already available in Computer. For example, a sales teammate can use a project’s existing account research and sales goals, follow a skill for writing outreach, and run a weekly automation to review the pipeline.

It brings those pieces together to identify stalled conversations, prepare follow-ups for review, and apply the results to the next week’s work.

Isolated environments and access controls

Teammates build on Computer’s existing tool and project permissions. Each teammate runs in a separate environment, with browser sessions separate from other teammates.

Saved credentials are encrypted and entered securely. Users can review completed work, take over the desktop, or redirect a teammate as it works.

Workflows across the business

Teammates handle ongoing work across business functions. These examples show how monitoring, investigation, and follow-through work together:

Marketing: A marketing teammate manages social posts, email campaigns, ads, search engine optimisation, and review notes, creating new ads based on what’s working. It monitors campaign performance and competitors’ promotions, drafts fixes when results slip, and suggests responses when competitors change prices.

Sales: A sales teammate finds opportunities in customer enquiries, past purchases, and unfinished conversations. It prepares outreach and quotes, follows up on replies, and flags support issues that need to be resolved before reaching out.

hn.titleZh: Perplexity 推出人工智慧工作代理
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
隊友是複雜、持續工作的代理人 Perplexity 於 2025 年 7 月在 Comet 瀏覽器中率先推出了第一個具有網絡功能的 AI 助手。它對於預訂餐廳、購物以及當今個人代理商流行的數十種用途非常有用。從那時起，模型功能取得了顯著進展。 Perplexity Computer 是數百萬人和公司利用準確的人工智慧進行認真工作的地方。個人代理需要專為工作而設計。今天，我們正在推出可以承擔這項長期工作的隊友、個人代理。他們規劃和協調項目，隨著優先事項的變化而改變方向，並提交結果供審查。使用者可以一路檢查和指導他們的工作。電腦可以處理複雜的項目，但設定代理來負責正在進行的工作需要規劃。團隊成員利用電腦的強大功能，並使用您的所有工具和文件在電腦內工作。一名隊友協調電腦會話和其他隊友以保持專案順利進行。他們在行銷、銷售、支援、營運或財務等不同工作流程中工作時會記住並學習。持續的專案所有權 Teammates 代表了一種使用 AI 的新方式。使用者可以將正在進行的操作委託給團隊成員，這樣人們就可以專注於結果，而不是協調每項任務。

基於 Perplexity 對準確性的關注和電腦的多模型功能，團隊成員可以規劃工作、檢查結果，並將完成的工作帶回進行審查。團隊成員可以調查問題、研究市場或測試產品的改進等任務。他們記住專案目標、任務歷史記錄以及運行期間的共用檔案。隊友承擔的每一項新任務都建立在已經完成的工作的基礎上。主動監控與跟進 隊友監控正在進行的工作並在情況發生變化時進行跟進。他們不等待新的詢問就進行調查並採取行動。例如，銷售團隊成員會注意到老客戶停止交易。隊友查看他們的訂單歷史記錄和支援問題並調查發生了什麼變化。然後，它會建立與該客戶相關的報價或標記在聯繫之前需要解決的任何問題。它共享進度更新和批准請求，直到完成工作。隊友也會記住過去的工作並將回饋應用於未來的任務。如果使用者告訴營運團隊成員某個機構需要提前兩週通知，則會將交付時間納入未來的專案計畫中。跨團隊分享方向 隊友可以跨團隊工作。將隊友加入 Slack 頻道，同事可以交給它工作或請求任務的更新。隊友也可以互相傳遞工作。

一名隊友發現網站上的錯誤，並將其發現傳遞給另一名隊友以準備修復。跨工具和任務的協調 隊友以電腦中已有的項目、技能和記憶為基礎。例如，銷售團隊成員可以使用專案的現有客戶研究和銷售目標，遵循撰寫外展的技能，並運行每週自動化來審查管道。它將這些碎片整合在一起，以識別停滯的對話，準備後續審查，並將結果應用到下週的工作中。隔離的環境和存取控制隊友建立在電腦現有的工具和項目權限之上。每個隊友都在單獨的環境中運行，瀏覽器會話與其他隊友分開。保存的憑證經過加密並安全輸入。使用者可以查看已完成的工作、接管桌面或在工作時重新導向團隊成員。跨業務的工作流程 團隊成員處理跨業務職能的持續工作。這些範例顯示了監控、調查和後續工作如何協同工作： 行銷：行銷團隊成員管理社群貼文、電子郵件行銷活動、廣告、搜尋引擎優化和審核筆記，根據有效內容建立新廣告。它監控活動績效和競爭對手的促銷活動，在結果下滑時草擬修復方案，並在競爭對手改變價格時提出應對措施。

銷售：銷售團隊成員在客戶詢問、過去的購買情況和未完成的對話中尋找機會。它準備外展和報價，跟進回复，並標記在外展之前需要解決的支援問題。客戶支援：客戶支援團隊成員審查前一天的投訴，總結趨勢，並標記需要執行長親自回覆的案例。它起草這些回复，跟進內部團隊的修復情況，並追蹤每個問題

hn.originalTitle: Ask HN: What hardware are you using to run local LLMs?
hn.sourceOriginalText:
Figured I'd ask here because I have no doubt some of you are running some pretty cool, cost effective solutions for local models. Don't doubt some have mini data centers in their closets either haha, but just looking to get a view into what fellow HN'ers are using for their day to day work.

Comment 1: I have a 3090 w/ 24G VRAM, it supports flash attention and bf16, but is a bit old. I dont run generative models on it as they would be slow and inaccurate, but I do run embedding models, OCR, and system one (decision) models on it.

Comment 2: I got pretty good results with my 3090 on Qwen 27b. Yeah, the rack is completely unusable when you launch the llm, but i wouldn't say its slow. Btw, fellow 3090 user, some time ago i saw this: https://github.com/Zagitta/gpu-unlock Can't try it personally because windows, but maybe it will help you.

Comment 3: OK, that gpu-unlock is something I've never seen before and...wow. I did some research and NVidia really did kneecap their RTX for market segmentation. Grrrrr

Comment 4: Wow, this seems to speed up inference by 68% or something for me. Holy shit.

hn.originalTitle: AI agents hallucinate prices: LLM grounding with live data
hn.sourceOriginalText:
LLM grounding tutorial: stop AI agents guessing prices

Ask an AI agent with no tools what a Kindle Paperwhite costs, and it can answer $159.99, the old launch price. The live price at the time of testing was $199.99. In tests, GPT-6 Luna and Claude Opus 5.5 each matched the live price exactly for 2 of 15 products from memory. With built-in web search, they gave more exact prices, but every run still had wrong prices, each with a source link.

Large language model (LLM) grounding is the standard way to stop both kinds of wrong price, from memory and from web search. A grounded agent answers only from data that it fetched for the question, and every answer shows where that data came from. For prices, a grounded agent needs live data, a clear status when a check fails, and code, not the model, that writes each price into the answer.

The Python agent below has each of these. It gets live prices from E-commerce Scraping Tool , a ready-to-run tool on the Apify marketplace. Apify calls these tools Actors. First, the tests show where wrong prices come from. Then you build the agent and test it step by step.

Why AI agents hallucinate prices

If your agent shows prices, a wrong one can reach your user in 3 main ways. The model answers from memory, it reads a bad page, or a tool says "ok" when it failed. The tests below check the first 2, on 21 live product pages from Amazon, Walmart, Best Buy, Target, and 4 Shopify stores. A research study tests the third.

The live prices come from E-commerce Scraping Tool, and an independent check with a separate scraping service, from US IP addresses, matched the Actor on all 21 pages. The results include only the 15 products with a single clear price for a new item, as a US shopper sees it without member discounts or coupons. A price is exact only when it matches the live price to the cent. The other 6 pages showed no price, or an unclear seller or size. The 15 prices didn't change while the models answered.

An LLM learns prices during training, and many of those prices change before a user asks. With no tools, gpt-6-luna and Claude Opus 5.5 gave these results. The last row adds the prompt "If you cannot know the current price, answer UNKNOWN":

Without the UNKNOWN prompt, Claude Opus 5.5 added a clear warning, such as "I can't check live prices," to all 21 answers. Each answer still included a price, and agent code reads the number, not the warning. So a prompt alone gave the user either a guess or nothing.

Prices can also change fast. The AirPods Pro 3 at Best Buy went from $199.99 to $249.99 in the 3 days before the models were asked. Even a price from last week can mislead your user.

When your agent fetches pages itself, the page can be the wrong one, even when it loads normally.

Wrong country. A request from outside the US received an Amazon page in Indian rupees. The model read it correctly and answered INR 7,503.02 for an Instant Pot that cost $79 in the US.

Wrong seller. An Amazon page showed "No featured offers available." The model answered $71.89. That price came from the line "Other sellers on Amazon New & Used (2) from $71.89," not from the Buy Box, the main offer on an Amazon page.

Wrong variant. Target redirected the link for the black Kindle Paperwhite to its parent product page, and Owala redirected its FreeSip link to the 32 oz size. A price from the new page can belong to another variant.

Code can detect each of these cases, because the data shows the currency, the seller, and the final page URL.

From a tool that says "ok" when it failed

The preprint Fabrication after tool failure , a study shared before peer review, tested what models do when a tool returns bad data. When the tool returned "ok" with bad data, such as an empty, outdated, or incomplete result, up to 45.3% of answers were dishonest. A dishonest answer hid the failure. When the tool returned an error status instead, the study reported 0% dishonest answers. So a price tool that reports a clear status or error helps the agent give honest answers.

What the 3 causes have in common

In all 3 causes, the wrong price looks like a normal answer, and nothing tells the user that something failed. The scraper tests show this. In 3 test runs, a simple do-it-yourself (DIY) scraper received 26 block pages. A block page is what a store shows when it blocks a request, such as Walmart's "Robot or human?" page or Amazon's "Continue shopping" page. The model answered "no price" for all 26. Those answers were honest, but the user still got no price. Every clearly wrong
hn.titleZh: 人工智慧代理產生價格幻覺：法學碩士以即時數據為基礎
hn.summaryZh: 這篇來自 Hacker News 工程師討論，重點和 LLM / Agent 有關。適合用來快速了解社群正在討論的實作方向、工具變化或使用心得。
hn.sourceTextZh:
LLM 基礎教學：阻止 AI 代理猜測價格 問一個沒有工具的 AI 代理 Kindle Paperwhite 的價格是多少，它可以回答 159.99 美元，即舊的發布價格。測試時的即時價格為 199.99 美元。在測試中，GPT-6 Luna 和 Claude Opus 5.5 均與記憶體中 15 個產品中的 2 個的即時價格完全匹配。透過內建的網路搜索，他們給出了更準確的價格，但每次運行仍然有錯誤的價格，每個價格都有一個來源連結。大語言模型 (LLM) 基礎是阻止記憶和網路搜尋中兩種錯誤價格的標準方法。接地代理僅根據為問題獲取的數據進行回答，並且每個答案都會顯示該數據的來源。對於價格，接地代理需要即時資料、檢查失敗時的清晰狀態，以及將每個價格寫入答案的程式碼（而不是模型）。下面的 Python 代理程式具有其中的每一個。它從 E-commerce Scraping Tool 獲取實時價格，E-commerce Scraping Tool 是 Apify 市場上的一個可立即運行的工具。 Apify 將這些工具稱為 Actor。首先，測試顯示錯誤的價格從何而來。然後您建立代理並逐步測試它。為什麼人工智慧代理會產生幻覺如果您的代理顯示價格，錯誤的價格可能會透過 3 種主要方式到達您的用戶。模型根據記憶進行回答，它讀取了錯誤的頁面，或者工具在失敗時說“正常”。

下面的測試檢查前 2 個，即來自 Amazon、Walmart、Best Buy、Target 和 4 個 Shopify 商店的 21 個即時產品頁面。一項研究測試了第三個。即時價格來自電子商務抓取工具，並使用單獨的抓取服務進行的獨立檢查來自美國 IP 位址，與所有 21 個頁面上的演員相符。結果僅包括 15 種新產品具有單一明確價格的產品，正如美國購物者所看到的，沒有會員折扣或優惠券。只有當即時價格與美分相符時，價格才是準確的。其他 6 頁沒有顯示價格，或不清楚的賣家或尺寸。 15款價格沒有變化，但型號有回應。法學碩士在培訓期間了解價格，其中許多價格在用戶詢問之前就發生了變化。在沒有工具的情況下，gpt-6-luna 和 Claude Opus 5.5 給出了這些結果。最後一行添加了提示「如果您無法知道當前價格，請回答 UNKNOWN」：在沒有 UNKNOWN 提示的情況下，Claude Opus 5.5 對所有 21 個答案添加了明確的警告，例如「我無法檢查實時價格」。每個答案仍然包含價格，代理代碼讀取的是數字，而不是警告。因此，單獨的提示要么給用戶一個猜測，要么什麼都沒有。價格也可能變化很快。在詢問型號之前的 3 天內，百思買的 AirPods Pro 3 從 199.99 美元漲到了 249.99 美元。即使是上週的價格也可能會誤導您的用戶。

當您的代理本身獲取頁面時，該頁面可能是錯誤的，即使它正常加載也是如此。錯誤的國家。來自美國境外的請求收到了以印度盧比顯示的亞馬遜頁面。該模型正確讀取並回答了速溶鍋的價格為 7,503.02 印度盧比，在美國售價為 79 美元。錯誤的賣家。亞馬遜頁面顯示「沒有可用的特色優惠」。該模特兒的回答為 71.89 美元。該價格來自「亞馬遜上的其他賣家全新和二手 (2) 起價 71.89 美元」這一行，而不是來自亞馬遜頁面上的主要報價「Buy Box」。錯誤的變體。 Target 將黑色 Kindle Paperwhite 的連結重定向到其父產品頁面，Owala 將其 FreeSip 連結重定向到 32 盎司尺寸。新頁面中的價格可以屬於另一個變體。程式碼可以偵測每種情況，因為數據顯示了貨幣、賣家和最終頁面 URL。工具失敗後說「ok」的工具 工具失敗後的預印本 Fabrication 是一項在同行評審之前分享的研究，測試了當工具傳回錯誤資料時模型會做什麼。當工具傳回「正常」且資料錯誤（例如結果為空、過時或不完整）時，高達 45.3% 的答案是不誠實的。不誠實的回答掩蓋了失敗。相反，當工具傳回錯誤狀態時，研究報告不誠實答案的比例為 0%。因此，報告明確狀態或錯誤的價格工具可以幫助代理商給出誠實的答案。

這 3 個原因的共同點 在所有 3 個原因中，錯誤的價格看起來像是正常的答案，並且沒有任何資訊告訴用戶某些事情失敗了。刮刀測試表明了這一點。在 3 次測試運行中，一個簡單的 DIY 抓取器收到了 26 個區塊頁面。封鎖頁面是商店封鎖請求時顯示的內容，例如沃爾瑪的「機器人還是人類？」頁面或亞馬遜的「繼續購物」頁面。該模型對所有 26 個答案都回答“無價格”。這些答案很誠實，但用戶仍然沒有得到價格。每一個明顯錯誤
